title: Big Bear Fire Abatement Letter? What to Do, Step by Step
desc: Got a weed abatement notice from Big Bear Fire? What the letter means, the clearance rules, deadlines, and how to pass inspection the first time.
h1: Got a Big Bear Fire Abatement Letter? Here's Exactly What to Do
answer_q: What should I do if I receive a weed abatement notice in Big Bear?
answer: Treat the letter as your official warning — Big Bear Fire Department is not required to send a separate violation notice before issuing a citation. Clear hazardous vegetation to the Priority Defensible Space standards (or hire help), keep photo documentation, and verify requirements on Big Bear Fire's website. Junk Removal Big Bear offers free on-site abatement quotes.
body:
Why you got the letter

Each year, Big Bear Fire Department mails abatement notices to property owners across the Valley — occupied homes and vacant lots alike. It isn't personal, and it doesn't necessarily mean your property was flagged as a problem: the notice states the defensible space standards every parcel must meet before fire season peaks. What makes it serious is the fine print: the notification letter is your warning. The department is not obligated to issue a separate notice of violation before citing you.

What the Fire Department expects, in plain English

  • 0–5 ft from structures: no pine needles, forest litter, dead vegetation, or combustible mulch — bare, ember-resistant ground
  • Within 15 ft: dry brush and high-energy-release vegetation removed near structures, propane tanks, hydrants and wood fencing
  • Whole property: forest litter thinned to about 2 inches depth (a thin layer stays for erosion control)
  • Roofs, gutters & decks: pine needles cleared from roofing, gutters, under and on decking, stairs and parking pads
  • Trees under 45 ft: lower limbs pruned up to 6 ft (max 25% of tree height)
  • Trees over 45 ft: limbed 12–15 ft up, and nothing within 10 ft of chimney openings

The full standards are on bigbearfire.org, and the department takes requests for defensible-space (AB 38) inspections — check its site to confirm current requirements for your parcel. Fawnskin (92333) is different: weed abatement and AB 38 inspections there are handled by San Bernardino County Fire, not Big Bear Fire. If cost is the obstacle, Big Bear Fire points owners to the Mountain Rim Fire Safe Council (firesafenow.org), which has had grant funding to help some owners with abatement notices — an application does not guarantee approval.

Your three options

Do it yourself. Doable for a small, flat lot — but budget full weekends, a truck for hauling, and transfer-station trips. The most common DIY failure isn't the clearing, it's the debris: piles left on the property don't count as abatement.

Hire a mow-and-blow crew. Cheaper per hour, but most leave the cut brush at your curb. You still own the hauling problem — and the deadline.

Hire a clearing + hauling service. One visit: cut, rake, prune, load, gone. This is what we do — and because we're a hauling company first, the debris leaves on our truck the same day.

If you're not on the mountain

A huge share of abatement notices go to second-home owners down the hill. You don't need to drive up: forward us the letter, send a few property photos on WhatsApp, approve the quote remotely, and you'll get before-and-after photos when the lot passes muster. Keep those photos — they're your proof of compliance if questions ever come up.

Don't wait for the inspection window

Abatement season compresses fast once letters land: crews book out, and the closer to inspection you start, the fewer options you have. The cheapest and calmest time to handle an abatement letter is the week it arrives.
faq: Is the abatement letter a citation?
No — it's the official warning that precedes one. Big Bear Fire is not required to send a separate notice of violation before citing a non-compliant property, so the letter itself is your deadline.
Do vacant lots have to be cleared too?
Yes. Priority defensible space requirements apply to vacant and unbuilt parcels as well as occupied properties, and vacant-lot owners receive the same notices.
Does Junk Removal Big Bear haul away the abatement debris?
Yes — clearing and haul-away happen in the same visit, so no brush piles are left at the curb. Free on-site quotes.

title: Where to Take Junk in Big Bear: Dump, Transfer Station & Pickup Options
desc: Big Bear Transfer Station location and hours, curbside bulky-item pickup, bear-safe trash rules, and when a haul-away service beats a dump run.
h1: Where to Take Junk in Big Bear: The Complete Local Disposal Guide
answer_q: Where is the dump in Big Bear?
answer: The Big Bear Transfer Station at 38550 Holcomb Valley Road (about 1.5 miles north of Baldwin Lake off Highway 18) accepts household waste, construction debris, yard waste, and tires — typically Monday–Saturday 8 AM–4:30 PM; confirm hours and fees on San Bernardino County's disposal sites page. For heavy or bulky loads, Junk Removal Big Bear offers pickup with free on-site quotes.
body:
Option 1: The Big Bear Transfer Station

The Valley's public drop-off is the Big Bear Transfer Station, 38550 Holcomb Valley Road — about 1.5 miles north of Baldwin Lake at Highway 18. It generally operates Monday–Saturday, 8 AM to 4:30 PM (closed Sunday) and accepts municipal solid waste, construction and demolition debris, yard waste, and auto tires. Hours, fees, and accepted materials change, so check the county disposal sites page before loading the truck.

What a dump run really costs: a vehicle that can haul it, tie-downs, disposal fees, and the round trip up Holcomb Valley Road — plus your Saturday. For one load of loose bags, fine. For a couch, a fridge, and half a garage? Do the math first.

Option 2: Curbside programs

Curbside options depend on where the property is:

  • City of Big Bear Lake (92315): Big Bear Disposal gives each residence one free curbside bulky-item pickup per year (up to 3 cubic yards or 4 large items); extra pickups cost a fee. Schedule through Big Bear Disposal. Bear-resistant carts are available for a one-time fee.
  • Big Bear City, Sugarloaf and Erwin Lake: the Big Bear City Community Services District (CSD) collects standard household bulky items curbside for a per-item fee, rents dumpsters, and holds periodic free community clean-up days. Details: Big Bear City CSD.
  • Clean Bear drop-off sites (41790 Garstin Dr and 39690 Big Bear Blvd) are only for residents and visitors staying in the City of Big Bear Lake, and only for bagged household trash and recycling — no bulky items, construction debris, or contractor loads.

Cart timing rules differ too: the City of Big Bear Lake prohibits leaving cans at the curb more than 24 hours, and the CSD allows carts out no more than 12 hours before collection and requires them back within 24 hours after.

Option 3: We come to you

For anything the free pickup won't cover — multiple items, heavy pieces, estate cleanouts, or the classic "the pile grew all summer" situation — a haul-away crew often makes more sense than people expect once dump fees, truck time, and a lost weekend are counted. Everything is loaded from wherever it sits (garage, deck, basement), and taken to a facility that accepts it.

What can't go in any of the above

Hazardous materials — paint, chemicals, motor oil, asbestos, propane tanks — can't go in curbside carts, our trucks, or regular transfer-station loads. San Bernardino County Fire runs household hazardous waste (HHW) collection; its Big Bear collection site is a government facility at the City of Big Bear Lake Public Works Yard (not a business address), normally open Saturdays. Hours and temporary closures change, so check with San Bernardino County Fire's HHW program before you go.
faq: Is the Big Bear dump open on Sunday?
The Big Bear Transfer Station is typically closed Sundays, operating Monday–Saturday 8 AM–4:30 PM — confirm current hours on San Bernardino County's disposal sites page before you go.
Does Big Bear have free bulky item pickup?

In the City of Big Bear Lake, Big Bear Disposal gives each residence one free curbside bulky-item pickup per year (up to 3 cubic yards or 4 large items) — see Big Bear Disposal's website. In Big Bear City, Sugarloaf and Erwin Lake, the Big Bear City CSD picks up bulky items for a per-item fee — see the CSD's website.
Should I do a dump run or hire junk removal?

For single small loads, the transfer station is cheapest. For bulky, heavy, or multi-item loads, full-service pickup is often comparable once disposal fees, truck rental, and time are counted — and the free on-site quote makes it easy to compare before deciding.

title: Hot Tub Removal in Big Bear: Process, Mountain Access & Cost Factors
desc: How hot tub and spa removal works on Big Bear's mountain lots: disconnection, cut-down, tight-deck access, and what affects the price. Free on-site quotes.
h1: Hot Tub Removal in Big Bear: What It Takes to Get a Dead Spa Off a Mountain Deck
answer_q: How does hot tub removal work in Big Bear?
answer: After a technician disconnects power and plumbing, the spa is drained, cut into sections, carried off the deck, and hauled for disposal — typically a half-day job on Big Bear's tiered decks and tight lots. Cost depends on spa size, deck access, and cut-down complexity, which is why Junk Removal Big Bear quotes every tub with a free on-site visit.
body:
Why Big Bear kills hot tubs

At 6,750+ feet, spas work harder than they do down the hill: hard freezes crack plumbing that wasn't winterized, snow loads stress covers and cabinets, and vacation-rental tubs run near-continuously through peak season. When one finally gives out, it becomes the heaviest piece of furniture on the property — 400 to 900 pounds dry — sitting on a deck that was built around it.

The removal process, step by step

  • 1. Disconnect: your electrician or spa tech kills the power (usually a 220V circuit) and caps the plumbing — required before any removal
  • 2. Drain: fully drained and left open to dry if possible
  • 3. Cut-down: most mountain tubs can't leave the way they arrived — decks got railed in, gates narrowed, trees grew — so we cut the shell into carryable sections
  • 4. Carry-out: sections and equipment pack are carried down stairs and switchback paths to the truck
  • 5. Haul & dispose: shell, cabinet, cover and pack are hauled the same visit
  • 6. Deck sweep: the footprint is swept clean — ready for a new spa or your new deck furniture

What affects the price

Three things, mostly: size (a 2-person tub is a different job than an 8-person swim spa), access (ground-level patio vs. a third-tier deck above a slope), and cut-down complexity (acrylic shells cut fast; older wood-cabinet and jetted concrete-adjacent installs take longer). Because these vary so much lot to lot in Big Bear, phone estimates for hot tubs are guesses — an on-site look isn't.

For vacation rental owners

A dead hot tub on an active STR listing costs bookings every week it sits there. We schedule tear-outs between guest stays, coordinate access through your property manager or lockbox, and send photos when the deck is clear — most tubs are gone within a day or two of the quote. Replacing rather than removing? We can also haul the old one the same day your new spa is delivered.
faq: Do I need to disconnect the hot tub before removal?
Yes — a licensed electrician or spa technician should disconnect the power and cap the plumbing first. After that, Junk Removal Big Bear handles draining, cut-down, carry-out, and disposal.
Can you remove a hot tub from a second-story or tiered deck?
Yes. Tight-access removals are standard in Big Bear: the tub is cut into sections and hand-carried down stairs and narrow paths — no crane needed for most lots.
How much does hot tub removal cost in Big Bear?

It depends on spa size, deck access, and cut-down complexity, so quotes are given free on-site: we look at the tub, quote a firm all-inclusive price, and can often start immediately. Text or WhatsApp us for one.

title: Big Bear Airbnb Host Turnover Checklist: Trash, Bulky Items & Compliance
desc: A turnover checklist for Big Bear Lake STR hosts: guest trash rules, the 24-hour container limit, furniture swaps, hot tub care and avoiding fines.
h1: The Big Bear Airbnb Host's Turnover Checklist (Beyond the Cleaning Crew)
answer_q: What do Big Bear Airbnb hosts need to handle between guests?
answer: Beyond standard cleaning, Big Bear Lake hosts must manage trash within city rules — containers can't sit on the street more than 24 hours around collection — plus bulky-item removal, furniture damage swaps, and hot tub upkeep. Operational violations start at $500. Junk Removal Big Bear handles the oversized side of turnovers with free on-site quotes.
body:
The part of turnovers your cleaner can't do

Big Bear Lake's vacation rental program has real enforcement: operational violations run $500 for a first offense, $1,000 for a second within 12 months, $1,500 for a third — and operating unlicensed starts at $1,500. Most of those violations trace back to the physical property: trash, parking, noise, occupancy. Your cleaning crew handles linens and surfaces; this checklist covers everything bigger. (Outside city limits — Big Bear City, Fawnskin, Sugarloaf — the County's short-term rental permit rules apply instead, including removing trash after each stay and using animal-proof containers.)

The between-stays checklist

  • Trash timing: containers out no more than 24 hours before/after collection — holiday-weekend overflow needs a pickup plan, not a prayer
  • Overflow bags: never stacked beside the bin (bears will find them before code enforcement does — and both are expensive)
  • Damaged furniture: photograph for the claim, then swap fast — a listing photo with a missing sofa costs bookings
  • Mattresses: replace on a schedule, not after the review that mentions the sag
  • Hot tub: drain-and-scrub on a cycle that matches occupancy, not the calendar
  • Deck & garage: clear of previous-owner storage and dead equipment before photography and license renewal
  • Guest-left items: bulky abandoned gear (broken sleds, coolers, chairs) out before the next check-in

Same-day windows are the whole game

Turnover work only counts if it fits between a morning checkout and an afternoon check-in. That's how we schedule: WhatsApp the job with your window, get a firm quote back fast, and the crew works inside the gap — lockbox or property-manager access, before/after photos when we lock up. Hosts and managers running multiple doors get priority scheduling and one point of contact for every property in the Valley.

The furniture swap play

The most efficient move for refreshes: schedule delivery of the new piece and removal of the old one for the same window. Old sofa out the day the new one arrives, packaging hauled — one visit, fewer days off-market.
faq: How long can trash containers stay out in Big Bear Lake?
City vacation-rental rules prohibit containers sitting on the street more than 24 hours before or after collection — a common source of operational violations, which start at $500.
Can you do a turnover pickup between guests?
Yes — same-day windows between checkout and check-in are the standard booking, seven days a week, with lockbox access and photo confirmation for remote hosts.
Do you work with property managers?
Yes. Management firms and co-hosts get priority scheduling and a single contact for all properties, with quotes approved remotely and documentation on every job.

title: Estate & Inherited Cabin Cleanouts in Big Bear: A Practical Guide
desc: Clearing an inherited cabin in Big Bear: where to start, sorting keepsakes and donations, remote coordination for families, and realtor timelines.
h1: Clearing an Inherited Cabin in Big Bear: A Practical, Humane Guide
answer_q: How do estate cleanouts work in Big Bear?
answer: A Big Bear estate cleanout typically runs in three passes: family keepsakes first, then donation-worthy items, then haul-away of the remainder — with the whole process manageable remotely for off-mountain families. Junk Removal Big Bear provides sorted, documented estate cleanouts with free on-site quotes.
body:
Start smaller than you think

Most Big Bear cabins that reach an estate cleanout hold decades of accumulation — the crawl space, the under-deck storage, the garage rafters. Trying to make every decision in one weekend is how families burn out. The approach that works is three passes, in order, with the easy decisions first.

The three-pass method

Pass 1 — Keepsakes. Family only. Photos, documents, and the personal items that matter. Take your time here; everything else can be delegated, this can't. Check every pocket, book, and coffee can — mountain cabins hide things.

Pass 2 — Donation & sale. Furniture in good shape, tools, working appliances, winter gear. In a resort town there's steady demand for used cabin furnishings; what doesn't sell locally donates well. Tell us what's going to family, sale or donation and we'll keep it separate from the haul-away.

Pass 3 — Everything else. This is the pass that overwhelms families and where a crew earns its fee: full-cabin loading, the heavy pieces down the loft ladder, the shed contents, the freezer nobody wants to open. Multi-load jobs get a firm written quote up front from the on-site walkthrough.

Managing it from down the hill

Most families we work with don't live on the mountain. The remote process: an on-site walkthrough scheduled with your realtor, lockbox, or a local relative; a firm quote with photos; approval and payment handled remotely; then documented progress photos and a broom-clean finish. For probate and fiduciary situations, ask for a written quote and before/after photos for the file.

If the cabin is headed to market

Realtors in the Valley list faster with an empty, clean cabin — buyers up here are imagining their own gear in the garage, not looking at someone else's. Typical timeline from walkthrough to broom-clean is days, not weeks, and we coordinate directly with your listing agent on access and deadlines, including escrow-driven ones.
faq: Can we handle an estate cleanout without traveling to Big Bear?
Yes. The walkthrough, quote, approval, payment, and completion photos can all be handled remotely, with access via your realtor, a lockbox, or a local contact.
What happens to items that are still usable?

By volume, quoted as a firm written price after a free on-site walkthrough — multi-load cabins included. Text or WhatsApp us to schedule one.
